forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 21%. No formal AGI claim over the weekend (7 Jun). Latest signals (KuCoin/business coverage 5-7 Jun) note Anthropic and DeepMind continue to emphasise self-improvement acceleration and that Anthropic reports >80% of code is AI-generated, but neither lab has issued an AGI declaration. Hassabis (Decrypt, early June) holds ~50% by 2030; Amodei holds 'within a few years' (2027 lean). Nothing in the last 48 hours moves the resolution probability.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires a credible public AGI claim from a major lab OR 3+ leading researchers stating AGI achieved, before 1 Jan 2030 (~3.5 yrs out). Definitional disputes raise the bar; labs historically defer transformational claims until capability is unambiguous.

factors_up.factor: Amodei (Anthropic) maintaining ~2027 AGI timeline; competitive pressure across 6+ frontier-tier labs
AI-automating-AI feedback loops (Anthropic >80% code AI-generated, DeepMind self-improvement comments)
Continued capability gains (Stanford AI Index 2026; HLE jump in past year)

factors_down.factor: No major lab has issued any formal AGI claim as of 7 June 2026
Definitional ambiguity raises bar for the '3+ senior researchers' clause
Hassabis (DeepMind) still anchoring ~50% by 2030 — not pre-2030

key_uncertainties: Whether internal capability translates to public AGI declarations before 2030
Whether IPO pressure on OpenAI/Anthropic incentivises or deters such claims
Pace of AI-automating-AI loops in 2027-2029
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from a frontier lab
Public statement by 2+ senior researchers at OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind that AGI is achieved
Major step-change on AGI-relevant evals (METR, HLE, ARC-AGI v3)

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 24%. Weekend reporting (Fast Company, FinalRoundAI, Inc) consolidates the picture: McKinsey ~3,000-4,000 cuts (~10% of workforce) in 2025-2026 with AI cited as primary driver; Bain, BCG, Deloitte slowing hiring or trimming headcount; LinkedIn Economic Graph 2026 review shows ~25% of consulting entry-level postings require AI fluency (vs <5% two years ago). Direction-of-travel signals consistent with prior reads but cumulative job declines remain <10% from 2024 baseline. 33% by 2030 still requires sustained acceleration. No change in central estimate.
forecasts.base_rate: 33% decline from 2024 baseline in revenue OR employment for economic consultancy by end-2030, attributed to AI by 2+ credible analyses. Historical industry shocks of this magnitude over ~6 years are rare outside structural recessions.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey ~10% headcount cut explicitly attributed to AI productivity gains
Entry-level pyramid collapse — junior analyst roles shrinking across Big 3
Fee compression as clients see AI-augmented productivity in their own teams

factors_down.factor: BCG growing in AI/tech specialist hiring — mix shift, not net contraction
AI-driven productivity often expands demand for advisory work in client transformations
33% in 4-5 years is steep; lagging definition of 'economic consultancy' makes resolution ambiguous

key_uncertainties: Definition of 'economic consultancy' (Big 3 strategy vs specialist econ houses vs Big 4 economics teams)
Whether AI displaces junior labour faster than it expands advisory mandates
Macro: a 2027-2028 recession could accelerate both displacement AND attribution
update_triggers: Big 3 reporting cumulative >15% headcount decline cumulatively
Top-line revenue decline of >10% YoY at 2+ majors with AI cited
FT/Economist analytical pieces explicitly framing the sector as collapsing

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 4%. Weekend PollCheck (6 Jun) 7-poll moving average: Reform 27.1%, Lab 18.4%, Con 18.1%, Grn 14.7%, LD 12.1%. Reform's lead widens marginally as Conservative-Labour neck-and-neck split for second place stabilises. Ipsos UK reaffirms ~6pt Reform lead. No improvement in Labour position; structural pattern since May 2025 unchanged. Path to largest party requires a ~10pt swing back to Labour over the next 3.5 years, with Reform losing both Conservative defectors and Labour's lost left-flank voters from Greens/LD.
forecasts.base_rate: Mid-term UK governments often recover 5-10pp by election day, but Labour starting deficit vs Reform is unusually large for an incumbent.

factors_up.factor: Reform's coalition includes ex-Tories who may revert; Labour core vote still has floor
Incumbency tools (fiscal levers, immigration policy) still available to PM
3.5 years is long — campaign dynamics, Reform leadership shocks possible

factors_down.factor: Reform consolidated ~27% for over a year — past stickiness threshold
Labour bleeding left flank to Greens and LDs as well as right to Reform
Sub-20% polling for an incumbent at mid-term historically points to seat collapse, not recovery

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform can convert poll lead to seats under FPTP
Whether a new centrist or technocratic vehicle emerges to fragment the right
Macro: 2027-2028 recovery could re-rate Labour competence
update_triggers: Labour back into low-20s in 7-poll average
Reform polling collapse (below 22%)
Major realignment event: party split, defections, leadership change at Labour or Reform

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. Weekend confirms continuity: Hassabis ~50% by 2030 implies substantial probability mass on 2030-2034; Amodei still anchoring near-term (2027); Anthropic >80% of code AI-generated reinforces self-improvement loop narrative. With ~8.5 years to resolution and three frontier labs all forecasting AGI within the window, central remains 78%.
forecasts.base_rate: 8.5 years is a long window; cumulative probability of AGI declaration scales with both capability growth and willingness of labs to claim it.

factors_up.factor: Three major labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind) all forecasting AGI within the window
AI-automating-AI feedback loops becoming visible (>80% Anthropic code AI-generated)
Continued capability gains on HLE, ARC-AGI, METR with no observed wall

factors_down.factor: Definitional disputes may delay formal claims even with capable systems
Macroeconomic or political shocks (compute restrictions, GPU crackdowns) could slow timelines
Past forecasters have over-anchored on lab timelines and been wrong

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling laws hold to 2030 without architectural breakthroughs
Whether 'AGI' will get redefined upward as capabilities increase
Geopolitical disruptions to compute supply chains
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from a major lab
Plateau in major eval performance over 6+ months
Compute supply chain shock

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. AEI China & Taiwan Update (5 Jun) and Focus Taiwan reporting note continuing PLA grey-zone activity but no new major exercise this week. December 2025 'Justice Mission-2025' established the rehearsal pattern for full maritime blockade. Latest US ODNI assessment continues to indicate Chinese leaders do not currently plan to execute an invasion of Taiwan. Taiwan's June defence budget and drone development reporting reflect deterrence posture. 3.5-year horizon with no observed acceleration in escalation triggers.
forecasts.base_rate: Base rate of full-scale military action (blockade >72hrs OR assault on Taiwan proper) in any given 4-year window since 1996 is low (~5-10%). PLA capability building is steep but Xi continues to prioritise economic stabilisation.

factors_up.factor: PLA capability investments continue to compress prep time for blockade option
'Justice Mission-2025' rehearsed full blockade — operational template exists
US distraction risk (Ukraine, Middle East, domestic) creates windows

factors_down.factor: US ODNI assessment: Chinese leaders do not currently plan invasion
China economic fragility (real estate, deflation, demographics) raises costs of war
No mobilisation indicators consistent with imminent action

key_uncertainties: Whether 2027 'Xi target year' narrative reflects intent or analyst projection
Whether US-China tariff/tech war escalation could trigger forcing function
Taiwan political dynamics — DPP vs KMT trajectory through 2028
update_triggers: PLA mobilisation indicators (mass reservist call-up, port closures, shipping rerouting)
Public Xi statement setting hard deadline
Direct US-PRC military incident in Strait or SCS

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 5%. Latest ONS print is April 2026 CPI at 2.8% (released May), down from March's 3.3% — moderation is real but the gap to <2.0% remains material. May 2026 CPI release scheduled mid-June. With only ~6 months of data points before the deadline, the path to a sub-2% print requires sustained downward surprises. Services inflation remains sticky; wage growth still ~4-5%. Probability remains low but non-trivial given the recent April moderation.
forecasts.base_rate: UK headline CPI has been above 2.0% for ~3 years; sub-2% prints have been rare outside disinflationary shocks.

factors_up.factor: April 2026 print 2.8%, down 50bp MoM — momentum clearly downward
Housing/energy base effects favourable in late 2026
Weak demand: GDP forecast 1.1% 2026; labour market loosening

factors_down.factor: Services inflation sticky at >4%, wages still elevated
Path from 2.8% to <2.0% in 6 months requires ~25bp/month decline — historically uncommon
BoE policy path conditional on inflation hold — fewer 'extra' disinflationary surprises priced in

key_uncertainties: Oil/energy price path through autumn 2026
GBP/USD trajectory and import price effects
Whether wage growth moderates faster than expected
update_triggers: May 2026 CPI print (mid-June) significantly below 2.5%
Wages YoY moderating below 3.5%
Sharp energy price decline

Marginal downward drift on softer Polymarket signal.

No Way Home precedent shows Spider-Man can clear $1.9B in this era
MCU Phase 6 anchor film with Punisher cameo + reset narrative

Avengers: Doomsday positioning compresses MCU revenue across films in 2026

Whether legs into Q4 hold up post-Avengers release
Critical reception — review embargo not yet lifted

China release confirmed/blocked
Polymarket back above 55% or below 35%

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. Weekend reporting (Sacra, Remio, MindStudio, Morningstar) consolidates the picture: Anthropic ~$45B ARR (gross of cloud-reseller basis) and OpenAI ~$33B ARR as of May/June 2026, combined ~$78B — already above $70B threshold using the most credible reporting methodologies. Even under OpenAI's lower-net Anthropic accounting (~$22B), combined ~$55B with sustained growth toward $70B by Dec 2026 highly likely. Resolution criterion explicitly allows credible reporting from FT/Bloomberg/The Information or company disclosures, all of which currently support the higher figure. Risk to resolution would be a severe Q4 demand collapse — not visible.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already >$70B on credible reporting (Anthropic $45B + OpenAI $33B)
IPO disclosure pressure forces high transparency on numbers
Enterprise deal pipeline expanding through year-end

factors_down.factor: Accounting methodology dispute may reduce headline Anthropic figure
Catastrophic compute outage or data incident could pause growth
Macro recession could trigger enterprise spending cuts in Q4

key_uncertainties: Whether 'credible reporting' converges on gross or net Anthropic ARR
Whether FT/Bloomberg/Information cite the higher or lower figure at year-end
Q4 2026 reporting cadence (pre- or post-IPO)

Anthropic revising ARR methodology downward
Compute supply disruption causing revenue impact

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 35%. OBR March 2026 EFO frames the central path: 1.1% in 2026, 1.6% in 2027, averaging 1.6% from 2027-2030 with productivity growth assumed to pick up to 1% medium-term. OBR's productivity scenarios show a 0.5% case (status quo since 2010) implies notably lower decade growth; 1.5% case (more optimistic AI-productivity scenario) implies meaningful upside. Decade average >1.5% requires sustained productivity rebound — plausible but not central. No new data this weekend; hold central.
forecasts.base_rate: UK decade-average real GDP growth has been below 1.5% across 2010s (~1.9% but mostly pre-Brexit), and 2020s on track for <1.5%. Productivity since 2008 has averaged ~0.5%.

factors_up.factor: AI-driven productivity uplift could lift 2030s growth above OBR central path
Net migration assumptions still adding to labour supply through 2030s
Catch-up potential from current low base if planning/investment reforms bite

factors_down.factor: Productivity averaged ~0.5% since 2008 — entrenched trend
OBR central forecast of 1.6% (2027-2030) leaves no margin for 2030s shocks
Ageing demographics drag on labour input from mid-2030s

key_uncertainties: Magnitude and timing of AI-driven productivity uplift
Net migration trajectory through 2030s
Energy cost and investment trajectory
update_triggers: OBR upgrading productivity assumption above 1.2%
Sustained productivity print >1.5% YoY for 4+ quarters
Material change in net migration assumptions
